rubric_definition: After you make the edit that one reviewer is asking for, does the other reviewer's comment still stand? If it is discharged too, the two findings are one defect; if it survives, they are different defects that share a location. If a reviewer offers two alternative fixes, either one discharging the other comment makes it one defect. Contradictory prescriptions to the same lines are different defects, because no single edit satisfies both.
evidence: A's defect is that the read-only negative test lacks a positive control proving the synthetic Ctrl-z would otherwise reach the keymap; B asks for a wholly new test exercising vim's routeVimHistoryToStore (u/<C-r> → store.undo/redo). Adding a positive control to the read-only test leaves B's missing vim-routing coverage unaddressed, and adding the vim routing test leaves A's unverified negative assertion intact — A's passing mention of the vim read-only fall-through is a different code path from B's command monkey-patching.

panel.finding_key: packages/notes/src/view/editor.test.ts::'leaves history unbound on a read-only mount' is a negative test with no positive control
panel.summary: 'leaves history unbound on a read-only mount' is a negative test with no positive control
panel.evidence: The test dispatches a Ctrl-z keydown on `.cm-content` of a read-only mount and asserts `store.getText()` is unchanged. Nothing in the test proves the synthetic keydown would ever have reached CodeMirror's keymap on this mount (no focus, editable=false, jsdom); the assertion also holds if the event is simply ignored for unrelated reasons, so it does not specifically demonstrate that `historyKeymap: readOnly ? [] : ...` is what suppressed the undo. It also never covers the vim read-only fall-through added in editor.ts:52-56.

coderabbit.evidence: **Add vim-mode coverage for `routeVimHistoryToStore`.** This block tests default-keymap history bindings (Mod-z / Mod-Shift-z). No test in the diff exercises `editor.ts`'s `routeVimHistoryToStore`, which routes vim's `u` / `<C-r>` to the store by monkey-patching `CodeMirror.commands.undo/redo`. This is new, module-scoped routing logic; a regression there would go undetected. Add a test that switches the editor to `vim` keymap and dispatches `u` / `<C-r>` (or calls `CodeMirror.commands.undo/redo` directly against the mounted view's `CodeMirror` instance) to confirm it reaches `store.undo()` / `store.redo()`.
